summary.en: The Colombian government opened an embassy in Jerusalem and launched a cultural counterrevolution that is removing more than thirty artworks from the National Museum and ordering the removal of LGBTQ2S+ political works. The mobile anti-riot police unit implicated in multiple killings has returned to operate in the country, and a preacher was killed by a criminal group in Cartagena. An earthquake in Colombia has left more than 224 dead and rescue operations continue, while a Colombian asylum seeker was tackled by ICE agents outside his home in Washington. 225 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Den colombianske regjeringen åpnet en ambassade i Jerusalem og igangsatte en kulturell motrevolusjon som fjerner mer enn tretti kunstverk fra Nasjonalmuseet og beordrer fjerning av LGBTQ2S+-politiske verk. Den mobile anti-opprørs politienheten som er involvert i flere drap, har kommet tilbake for å operere i landet, og en predikant ble drept av en kriminell gruppe i Cartagena. Et jordskjelv i Colombia har etterlatt mer enn 224 døde og redningsarbeidet pågår, mens en colombiansk asylsøker ble taklet av ICE-agenter utenfor hjemmet sitt i Washington. 225 kamprelaterte dødsfall ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Colombian conflict
background.extract: The Colombian conflict began on May 27, 1964, and is a low-intensity asymmetric war between the government of Colombia, paramilitary groups, crime syndicates, and far-left guerrilla groups engaged in armed factional hostilities to increase their influence in Colombian territory. Some of the most important international contributors to the Colombian conflict include multinational corporations, the United States, Cuba, and the drug trafficking industry.
